transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Start: 17:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Ethan Brooks, Lena Ortiz, Kai Nakamura, Owen Clarke + company all-hands

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Leadership presents a short framework for faster, clearer decisions.
- Hiring and runway update: adjust cadence, pause for critical IC hiring.
- SLA/incident updates: better on-call rotations, runbook edits, clearer customer communication templates.
- Product: small, measurable changes to default batching and cache behavior to lower unit cost without breaking latency SLAs.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone. thank you for joining the all-hands, really appreciate the time. we'll try to keep this tight — we have about an hour. good to see so many faces. quick housekeeping, this is recorded and will be shared.

00:18 Maya: Quick agenda — decision framework, runway/hiring, ops & SLA updates, product changes for efficiency, then Q and A. Ethan's gonna walk a couple of the infra points.

00:28 Ethan: hi folks. hi. so first, decision framework. we have been hearing that teams are stuck awaiting cross-org approvals and that is killing velocity. we want to move to a 3-tier model — "single-owner decisions" for low-risk things, "leader-reviewed" for medium scope, and "governed" for high risk things that touch infra, security, or external contracts. the idea is to reduce "deferred" decisions.

00:58 Audience Member 1: uh, quick clarifying q — what qualifies as high risk?

01:02 Ethan: yes. anything that changes customer facing SLAs, data residency, encryption, external contractual terms, or significant spend increases — those are governed. medium is, like, infra tweaks that change autoscaling or routing by more than, say, 20 percent. single-owner is, um, day-to-day product UX or bug fixes. it's deliberately pragmatic.

01:28 Maya: to add, we will publish a matrix in the handbook this week with examples. if you're unsure, flag it and we'll advise. but we want teams to move faster, trust people closer to the problem, and track decisions asynchronously.

01:45 Lena: and to that point, product will start a "decision log" page for cross-functional items so folks can see who signed off and the rationale. that will help retros and audits.

02:02 Kai: quick ops note: incident runbooks — we've had two flaps this quarter where on-call handoffs were unclear. we're standardizing the runbook layout, and adding a very short SLA-comms template so Customer Success and Sales have a consistent message during incidents.

02:22 Owen: financial/regret note — we are near plan on ARR but CTO and product-led experiments cost us some headroom. we plan to be conservative with hiring until we see the first two months of the Q4 pipeline convert. that means we will prioritize critical IC roles over general headcount.

02:43 Maya: yes — the ask here is that managers re-evaluate open reqs and tag them as Critical / Nice-to-have by Friday. we'll share the updated hiring cadence Friday end of day.

03:00 Audience Member 2: is this a hiring freeze? or just prioritization?

03:03 Owen: not a strict freeze, more a prioritization. critical roles still move, but we'll tighten approval for new team expansions.

03:18 Ethan: on the infra front: three concrete items — one, we are rolling out a canary change to batching defaults to lower per-token cost; two, improving prefix/K V cache heuristics — our transcription sometimes says K V cash, but it's KV cache — and three, we will enable a default autoscaler safe mode for dedicated clusters so we don't overburst and blow spend.

03:46 Lena: the batching canary is low-risk, paired with tighter traces so we can rollback quickly if regen rates spike. we expect a 6-12% unit-cost improvement in average workloads.

04:04 Ethan: caveat — for latency-sensitive flows we will not change defaults. teams owning low-latency product routes should opt in to keep current settings. we will publish a compatibility matrix.

04:18 Audience Member 3: are there benchmarks we can see?

04:21 Ethan: yes, we'll post the canary dashboard link and the raw traces. I want to be clear: this is about cost-per-token not model quality. if we see upstream regressions we'll stop it.

04:34 Maya: on security/compliance — we've completed the SOC 2 gap review and are starting a third-party pen test next month. we also added more KMS rotation guidance; our security team will share a short FAQ for engineering and solutions, because questions about KMS, HSM, and key cust — sorry, key custody — keep popping up.

04:58 Kai: as part of the runbook work we'll add an on-call rota that maps to team SLOs. also better paging thresholds so we reduce noisy pings.

05:12 Audience Member 4: will the updated runbook affect who gets paged for dedicated/private deployments?

05:18 Kai: short answer: yes. dedicated/private deployments will have an explicit escalation path and a customer-liaison role so we don't have the usual finger-pointing during incidents.

05:30 Maya: moving to culture for a second — trust and asynchronous communication. we three leaders want to be explicit that we value dissent, but we also need decisions to be recorded and made. that means more concise PRDs, decision notes in the new log, and explicit owners.

05:48 Ethan: and on that note, we'll pilot a "decision hour" on Tuesdays where leaders will triage pending cross-org approvals so we don't leave things in limbo for weeks.

06:02 Audience Murmur / Applause

06:08 Maya: ok quick shoutouts — eng shipped a noisy but important telemetry pipeline fix last week, ops stabilized pod evictions on dedicated clusters, and product delivered the rerank API improvements earlier than planned. thank you to those squads.

06:25 Maya: now, Q and A. please drop questions in the Q&A or raise hand, we'll take a few.

06:31 Audience Member 5: hey, onboarding question — with the hiring changes, will new ICs still get the same ramp plan?

06:36 Lena: yes, ramp plans remain; we might stagger cohort start dates to match mentors' availability but the content is unchanged.

06:45 Audience Member 6: regarding the batching change — will this affect embeddings? we have a large offline embeddings job that is cost heavy.

06:52 Ethan: embeddings offline jobs are separate — we'll include batching knobs for offline jobs in the canary. the immediate defaults affect online generation paths. embeddings large jobs we will recommend different concurrency and chunk sizes.

07:08 Audience Member 7: a question about third-party pen tests — will customers get a summary report?

07:12 Maya: yes — the exec summary will be shareable. we won't publish the full report but customers with an NDA or who are in dedicated/private contracts will be able to see more detail.

07:22 Audience Member 8: any changes to data retention?

07:26 Owen: no broad changes planned. for hosted API we still retain metadata as per policy; for dedicated/private we're aligning docs so customers can set retention per their contracts.

07:40 Ethan: a small note — routing policies will become more transparent in the console. teams will be able to set region preference, cost tier, and have automated fallback. this ties back to the decision categories because routing changes that materially impact cost will be in the medium bucket.

07:58 Audience Member 9: are we still planning the APAC node expansion next quarter?

08:02 Maya: yes, but capacity scheduling will be more conservative. expansion remains a priority for next year, but we'll pace it against committed demand.

08:12 Audience Member 10: any update on the Dedicated pricing model?

08:16 Owen: we're iterating. there will be clearer burst credits and a new entry-tier for SMB customers to try Dedicated with smaller commitments. we'll share the pricing paper next week.

08:30 Maya: ok we're at the 40-minute mark so a quick final section — leadership commitments. 1) publish the decision matrix and decision-log starter by EOD Friday; 2) update and publish runbook and SLA templates by Dec 1; 3) managers tag hiring reqs by Friday. those are the three concrete things.

08:52 Audience applause

08:56 Maya: last quick thing — a small demo from product on the canary dashboard, Lena? 2-3 minutes.

09:02 Lena: sure. I'll share a quick view — um, so the canary shows request-level latency, regen-rate, token cost delta, and a small distribution chart. here you can see the 95th p95 — er, 95th latency is flat for the last 48 hours. token-cost is down 7 percent. we'll post the dashboard link in #announcements.

09:30 Audience Member 11: will we get an offline doc of the canary runbook?

09:33 Lena: yes, the canary playbook and rollback checklist will be in the handbook.

09:40 Maya: ok, thank you all. I'm really proud of the work and the focus here. quick recap of next steps and then we'll close.

09:48 Maya: recap — decision matrix & log by Friday, runbook/SLA by Dec 1, hiring tags by Friday, canary metrics posted and product to share playbook. if you have follow-ups, drop them in #leadership-questions or email me.

09:58 Audience Member 12: thanks. appreciate the transparency.

10:02 Maya: thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.

(Transcript end)

Notes on transcription fidelity: some technical terms were auto-corrected ("K V cache" -> KV cache, "ess el ay" -> SLA). There are several places with brief crosstalk and applause markers. Links referenced: canary dashboard (link posted in #announcements), decision matrix (handbook page to be published).
